clue.text: It sounds out of breath to me

definitions.note: the definition is a thing that sounds, that is, measures the depth of water

indicators.note: made out of means these letters are the raw material, reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: Someone says a noise strikes them as being caused by panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is the anagram signal: BREATH, TO and ME are rearranged. 'sounds' looks like a verb about noise, but here it means plumbs the depth of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument takes soundings, measuring how deep the water is beneath a ship.

clue.text: It makes a bundle for the farmer!

definitions.text: It makes a bundle for the farmer!

parts.words: It makes a bundle for the farmer!
parts.note: making a bundle suggests earning a fortune, but here it is a machine that literally packs hay into bundles

explanation.definitionFit: A farm machine that compresses hay or straw into tied blocks.

clue.text: Maximum storm capacity?

parts.note: the idiom a storm in a teacup means a fuss about nothing, so the most a storm can occupy is the cup's measure

explanation.definitionFit: The amount a small cup for tea holds, as a measure.

clue.text: It enables one to see things through other people's eyes

definitions.text: It enables one to see things through other people's eyes

parts.words: It enables one to see things through other people's eyes
parts.note: seeing through others' eyes suggests empathy, but here a doctor literally looks through the pupil into a patient's eye

explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that doctors use to examine the retina and interior of a patient's eye.

clue.text: Vertical technique, with boundaries all round…

indicators.note: the boundaries are wrapped all round the word for technique

parts.note: ends are boundaries or limits
a way is a method or technique

explanation.surface: An upright method is fenced in on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' wraps the boundaries round the technique, splitting the outer word after its third letter. 'Vertical' is fair: something set endways stands on its end, upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing on end, upright rather than lying flat.

clue.text: … permit England's openers to take championship

indicators.note: the opening letters of the word England's are taken

parts.note: a title is a sporting championship

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, England's opening batsmen are allowed to win the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 4 Down for the surface only. Here 'openers' takes the first two letters, EN, of England's.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a right to do something is to allow it.

clue.text: Ladies' society put on "The King and I" — it gets the bird

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, as if put on top in the written order

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
taken as written
WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's society

explanation.surface: A women's club stages the musical The King and I and is booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women, famous for amateur events. 'gets the bird' sounds like being booed, but the bird is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless bird native to New Zealand, its national emblem.

clue.text: Motionless in airliner taking off

indicators.note: the answer is found within the words airliner taking

explanation.surface: Passengers sit still in a plane during take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the run of letters inside airl(INER T)aking; 'taking off' is only surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Without movement or power to move, still.

clue.text: Number in sea off Cowes, not keeping heads above water

annotationWithheld.why: Number in sea off Cowes, not keeping heads above water (9): the parse is IN + V (number) in SOLENT (sea off Cowes), so 'in' would have to give the letters IN and also be the container signal putting V inside SOLENT, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Number in sea off Cowes, not keeping heads above water

clue.text: Pisa's tower, as such, is protected from demolition

definitions.meaning: the tower of Pisa is a leaning building, and listing means leaning
a building on an official heritage register that may not be pulled down

explanation.walkthrough: A ship that lists leans to one side, so the leaning tower is a 'listed' building in the punning sense. In Britain a listed building is one officially protected for its heritage.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure on the British heritage register, legally shielded from alteration; punningly, any leaning edifice.

clue.text: Found disgusting article in cargo

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the word for cargo

parts.note: a load is a cargo carried by a vehicle
the definite article is THE

explanation.surface: Customs officers come across something revolting packed in a shipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like 'discovered', but it belongs with 'disgusting' as the definition: something one found disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to consider it repellent, a past-tense verb matching found.

clue.text: Church, in outings, shows muscle

indicators.note: the church abbreviation sits inside the word for outings

parts.note: trips are excursions or outings
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A congregation's excursions show off its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-headed arm muscle at the back of the upper arm, which straightens the elbow.

clue.text: Outlined plan for coarse plaster

definitions.meaning: a roughly sketched draft or preliminary model
a wall coating of lime mixed with gravel or pebbles

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rough first draft of a scheme and a pebbly exterior wall rendering.

clue.text: Undisputed sum?

definitions.meaning: complete and absolute, as in an utter victory nobody can contest
the amount reached by adding figures together

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or absolute; as a noun it is the result of addition.

clue.text: Refuse decomposing alongside a lake

parts.note: food that is going rotten is said to be off
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads like a verb (to decline) but is the noun meaning waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails of a butchered animal, historically the waste parts thrown away.

clue.text: Mr Quelch, for example, was such a good painter!

definitions.meaning: Mr Quelch is the stern form teacher at Greyfriars school in the Billy Bunter stories, a schoolmaster of former days
a great European painter from before about 1800, such as Rembrandt

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Quelch is the schoolmaster in the Billy Bunter stories, popular British school fiction of the 20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-1800 artist of great skill, or punningly an elderly schoolteacher.

clue.text: Speed can't unsettle such clever footwork

indicators.note: to unsettle the letters is to disturb their order and rearrange them

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters CANT

explanation.surface: Dancers note that haste cannot spoil nimble steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettle' is the anagram signal working on SPEED and CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo dance performed with intricate steps, such as clog or tap dancing, prized for nimble feet.

clue.text: In action, a potentially harmful plant

indicators.note: potentially means these letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant that may cause harm when it is active.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' signals an anagram of IN ACTION A.
explanation.definitionFit: The tobacco genus, a family of flowering herbs whose leaves contain toxic nicotine.

clue.text: Affecting old man, it's a dilemma at traffic-lights

indicators.note: affecting means putting on a false manner, so these letters are disguised by rearranging them

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving the letters ITS

explanation.surface: An elderly man is troubled by a problem at a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is red-green colour blindness, named after the chemist John Dalton, who had it; 'traffic-lights' is the definition's telling detail, not a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Colour blindness, especially the inability to tell red from green, makes signals at a junction hard to read.

clue.text: Put heavily on the canvas, I am finished with the ring

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
past means over or finished
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A boxer flattened onto the mat says he is done with boxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' suggests a boxing ring's floor, but it is an artist's canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint laid on thickly so brush strokes stand out from the surface.

clue.text: These mimics, when put on, bring bad luck

definitions.meaning: people who imitate or ridicule others

definitions.text: when put on, bring bad luck

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put the mockers on' is a British idiom meaning to jinx or spoil something.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally those who mimic in derision; in the idiom, a jinx that spoils a plan.

clue.text: Like a girl's best friend before acquiring polish?

definitions.text: Like a girl's best friend before acquiring polish?

parts.words: Like a girl's best friend before acquiring polish?
parts.note: diamonds are a girl's best friend, and a gem before polishing has not yet been faceted by a jeweller

explanation.definitionFit: A rough gemstone that has not yet been shaped and faceted is described this way.

clue.text: Story, we hear, of such refined wit

definitions.meaning: story sounds like storey, a floor of a building; the top floor under the roof is the one meant
Athenian wit was proverbially elegant and delicate

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a homophone: 'story' sounds like 'storey', and the room under the roof is a storey of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a top-floor room, a storey; as an adjective it means Athenian, hence classically elegant.

clue.text: A piece of baggage turned up in Oklahoma

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: baggage is an old derogatory term for a disreputable woman, as is slut

explanation.surface: A suitcase surfaces somewhere in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses A and SLUT together, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the US state, so the clue describes a place found there.

clue.text: Gambler loses head, becomes a thief

indicators.note: the word's first letter is dropped, as if beheaded

parts.note: a speculator gambles on markets

explanation.surface: A punter down on his luck turns to stealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' removes the first letter of SPECULATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who embezzles public or entrusted money, a kind of thief.

clue.text: Tied up with bloody work inside

indicators.note: the word for work goes inside the colour

parts.note: blood is red
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone is bound up while gory work happens indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: OP (opus) is a standard abbreviation for a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound with cord, like cattle secured with a lasso.

clue.text: Oedipus's trouble takes up one page in stories

indicators.note: one page goes inside the word for stories

parts.note: tales are stories
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A Greek tragic hero's misfortune fills a page of a storybook.
explanation.walkthrough: Oedipus means 'swollen foot': he was lamed as a baby, so his trouble was a foot deformity.
explanation.definitionFit: Club foot, a congenital deformity of the foot, fitting the Greek name meaning swollen foot.

clue.text: Skin of peach found in mince-pie? Complain!

indicators.note: the first letters are found within the word mince-pie

parts.note: to carp is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone finds fruit peel in their Christmas pastry and grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' picks EPI out of minc(E-PI)e.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the outer layer of a fruit, its peel.

clue.text: Nothing in the farm butter range

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the animal that butts

parts.note: a ram is a farm animal that butts with its horns
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in the dairy's butter selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' reads as the spread, but it means one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander freely over an area is to range across it.

clue.text: Watch found on the beach

parts.note: a watch here is a body of people keeping lookout, posted along the shore rather than a timepiece dropped in the sand

explanation.definitionFit: This service keeps lookout along the shore to help vessels in trouble.
